title: Epigenetic regulation in early embryo development: from zygotic genome activation to the first lineage specification
source_note: Not the full paper: no access to the full text, so these notes are based only on the publicly available abstract and metadata (PubMed). Details from the main text and figures are missing.

items.q: What kind of paper is this and where was it published?
items.a: It is a review by Xu R, Li Y, Wu Y, Liu X and Gao S, published in Trends in Genetics in 2025.
items.info: PMID 40480920. These notes are based only on the abstract and metadata because the full text was not accessible.

items.q: What role does epigenetic regulation play in early embryo development?
items.a: It plays a pivotal role in orchestrating early embryo development and guides the transition from a totipotent zygote to a complex multicellular organism.

items.q: Which developmental window does the review focus on?
items.a: The dynamic landscape of epigenetic reprogramming during preimplantation embryo development, from zygotic genome activation (ZGA) to the first lineage specification.
items.info: The window is taken from the title and the keywords. The abstract does not say which species are covered. The MeSH terms list Humans and Animals.

items.q: Which epigenetic layers does the review cover?
items.a: DNA methylation, histone modifications, higher-order chromatin, transposable elements (TEs) and RNA modifications.
items.info: The review stresses how these layers interact with each other, not each one on its own.

items.q: What is the goal of epigenetic reprogramming in the early embryo, according to the review?
items.a: Resetting the parental epigenome, which comes about through the interplay of DNA methylation, histone modifications, higher-order chromatin, TEs and RNA modifications.
items.info: The abstract gives no details about the specific mechanisms.
items.concl: Resetting the parental epigenome depends on several epigenetic layers acting together.

items.q: In which artificial settings does the review discuss abnormal epigenetic reprogramming?
items.a: In somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) and in assisted reproductive technologies (ART).
items.info: The abstract does not say which specific defects are described.

items.q: Does the review link epigenetic defects to disease?
items.a: Yes. It summarizes clinical disorders that result from abnormal epigenetic reprogramming and discusses possible therapeutic strategies.
items.info: The abstract does not name the disorders or the therapeutic strategies.

items.q: What is the overall aim of the review?
items.a: To clarify the role of epigenetic modifications in developmental defects and to offer perspectives that help both developmental biology research and the clinical use of assisted reproduction.
items.info: The review also discusses future research directions.
items.concl: The review connects basic epigenetic reprogramming in early embryos with clinical problems in ART and SCNT.

items.text: Get the full text to check which species are covered, especially whether zebrafish or other non-mammalian models are discussed alongside the mammalian preimplantation embryo, and how TEs and RNA modifications act at ZGA.
